                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Ulnar nerve
opb. Anterior interosseous nerve
opc. Superficial radial nerve
opd. Posterior interosseous nerve
ope. Musculocutaneous nerve

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of forearm pain and weakness, marked weakness in finger extension, and radial deviation on wrist extension without sensory impairment are consistent with posterior interosseous nerve involvement. This nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, is responsible for motor innervation to the extensor muscles of the forearm, which explains the weakness in finger extension and radial deviation. The tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle aligns with the anatomical course of the posterior interosseous nerve, which can be affected by compression or injury in this region. The history of ulnar shaft fracture and surgical treatment could have led to changes in the forearm structure, potentially affecting the posterior interosseous nerve. The retrieved evidence path supports the involvement of the posterior interosseous nerve by linking nerve-related processes to the symptoms of asthenia (weakness). Therefore, the posterior interosseous nerve is the most likely affected nerve in this patient.
